newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Pro-China group offers world free TV of HK97 party.
newsitem.headline: Pro-China group offers world free TV of HK97 party.

text.p: A pro-Beijing group celebrating Hong Kong's return to China on July 1 is offering the world nearly 100 hours of free live television feeds to counter "negative reporting", the organisation said on Wednesday.
The Association for the Celebration of Reunification of Hong Kong with China will beam the June 29-July 3 handover festivities live by satellite to stations and viewers worldwide.
"We provide an alternative. People overseas can see how Hong Kong people see the future of Hong Kong," a spokeswoman said.
"We also hope to have interviews with leaders of the Chinese government and future Hong Kong government as well as common people on their views and aspirations," she said.
The organisation also plans to wrap footage from Hong Kong television stations into its 96-hour non-stop broadcast.
Hong Kong, a British colony of over 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight June 30.
An army of foreign reporters has taken up positions to cover what is dubbed Asia's "party of the century". More than 7,000 journalists have applied to attend the event.
But pro-Beijing groups and the government-in-waiting in Hong Kong fear the media are portraying only a doom-and-gloom side of the territory's sovereignty change.

One of the prime movers behind the offer is the association's publicity chief Rita Fan, who is also president of an appointed provisional legislature that China plans to install on July 1 to replace the elected Legislative Council.
The Association's broadcast starts at 10 p.m. local time (1400 GMT) on June 29 and Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd is sponsoring part of its satellite link.
"Hongkong Telecoms will sponsor the uplink (to satellite)... but television stations overseas which want to downlink will have to settle that themselves," the spokeswoman said.
"But they will not need to pay us anything."
Some local broadcasting stations such as Television Broadcasts Ltd, Wharf Cable and Radio Television Hong Kong are also offering free footage of their coverage of the gala party.
